body.x: RAONARK Inc. (CEO Koo, Min Ghi) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

RAONARK is a startup specializing in developing smart locks. Since its inception in 2020, professionals from Irevo (Gateman), a long-time leader in the digital door lock market in South Korea, gathered together as one team. Equipped with extensive expertise, RAONARK is considered to possess unparalleled know-hows among startups in the industry, launching its proprietary brand KeyIn to offer various smart lock solutions.

In this CES, RAONARK presented its smart-locks and the technologies which include 1) instant lock to eliminate security vulnerabilities, 2) smart safety ring to root out concerns over hacking, 3) motionless handle door lock powered by fully automated mortise. Such technology and products of the structural innovation solved the security vulnerabilities of existing smart locks, according to the business.

Since all these products come with patented door sensors built-in, no additional devices are necessary to autonomously sense if the door is locked or unlocked. In addition, they support smart home eco system that can be associated with smart and IoT devices, and can be custom-installed depending on the door size and environment. Furthermore, strong torque is applied to prevent the warping that happens on old wooden doors.

As for their reason for participating in this event, a RAONARK representative explained, “As diverse global businesses and investors gather together, we are looking for ODM customers, distribution channel partners, and investors.” They added, “With our technological excellence and competitiveness recognized by the three innovation awards, we have high hopes for the possibilities of reaching into the global markets.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
